contentObjective: I can explain a percent as a rate per 100, model it on a decimal grid or tape diagram, and interpret percents greater than 100%.

vocabulary.definition: A percent is a ratio that compares a number to 100, so every percent answers the question “how many out of 100?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje es una razón que compara un número con 100, así que todo porcentaje responde “¿cuántos de cada 100?”
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio comparing a number to 100 is a ___.

examples.text: 65 shaded squares out of a 100-square grid is 65%
examples.why: It compares the part to a whole of exactly 100.
The whole is not 100, so the count is not the percent.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio that compares a number to 100. The word means “per hundred,” and the symbol is %.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara un número con 100. La palabra significa “por cada cien” y su símbolo es %.
vocabulary.cloze: The word that means “per hundred” is ___.

examples.text: 9 out of 100 students walk to school → 9%
examples.why: The comparison is already out of 100.

vocabulary.definition: A comparison of one part against the whole amount. In a percent, the whole is always 100%.

vocabulary.definition: More than one whole. A percent above 100 means the amount is larger than the thing it is being compared to.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Car Sales
revealWordProblem.text:
A car dealership's sales for one month are shown in the monthly sales report. The owner now needs to order 50 cars from the factory.
Question: Based on the sales shown, how many of each type of car do you recommend the owner order?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A monthly sales report bar graph out of 100 cars sold: 8 hybrid, 18 all-electric, and 74 gas-powered.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Out of 100 cars sold, 8 were hybrid, 18 were all-electric, and 74 were gas-powered, so those counts are already percents: 8%, 18%, and 74%. Apply each percent to the 50-car order: 8% of 50 = 4 hybrids, 18% of 50 = 9 all-electric, and 74% of 50 = 37 gas-powered. That accounts for all 50 cars (4 + 9 + 37 = 50), so I recommend ordering 4, 9, and 37.

questions.stem: What does the word percent mean?
questions.explanation: Percent means per hundred, which is why every percent can be written as a fraction with a denominator of 100.
choiceFeedback: Per ten would be a tenth, not a percent.
Per thousand is a different comparison entirely.
"Part" does not say how big the whole is; a percent always compares to 100.
hints: Look at the second half of the word: cent.
A century is 100 years; a cent is 1/100 of a dollar.
Percent = per 100.
questions.explanationEs: Por ciento significa por cada cien, y por eso todo porcentaje se puede escribir como una fracción con denominador 100.
hintsEs: Mira la segunda parte de la palabra: ciento.
Un siglo son 100 años; un centavo es 1/100 de dólar.
Por ciento = por cada 100.

questions.stem: 3 out of every 10 students walk to school. What percent is that?
questions.explanation: Multiply both terms of the ratio by 10 to compare to 100: 3 out of 10 becomes 30 out of 100, or 30%.
choiceFeedback: 3 out of 100 would be 3%, but the ratio here is out of 10.
10 is the second term of the original ratio, not the percent.
That adds the two numbers instead of scaling the ratio.
hints: A percent compares to 100, so rewrite the ratio out of 100.
What do you multiply 10 by to get 100?
Multiply BOTH terms by that same number.
questions.stemEs: 3 de cada 10 estudiantes caminan a la escuela. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
questions.explanationEs: Multiplica los dos términos de la razón por 10 para compararla con 100: 3 de 10 se convierte en 30 de 100, o sea 30%.
hintsEs: Un porcentaje compara con 100, así que reescribe la razón sobre 100.
¿Por cuánto multiplicas 10 para obtener 100?
Multiplica AMBOS términos por ese mismo número.

questions.stem: A decimal grid has 100 squares and 65 are shaded. What percent is shaded?
questions.explanation: Each square is one percent, so 65 shaded squares is 65%.
choiceFeedback: This is ten times too small — moving the decimal one extra place shrinks the real percent down to this.
35 is the number of UNshaded squares.
100% would mean every square is shaded.
hints: How many squares are in the whole grid?
Each square stands for 1%.
Count the shaded squares.
questions.stemEs: Una cuadrícula decimal tiene 100 cuadros y 65 están sombreados. ¿Qué porcentaje está sombreado?
questions.explanationEs: Cada cuadro es un por ciento, así que 65 cuadros sombreados son 65%.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos cuadros hay en toda la cuadrícula?
Cada cuadro representa 1%.
Cuenta los cuadros sombreados.

reviewHighlights.formula: Percent = Parts per 100 = Ratio of a number to 100
steps: 3. Fraction to Percent: Scale fraction to a denominator of 100
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake with percent is scaling only one term of the ratio: reading 7 out of 10 as 7%. A percent compares to 100, so BOTH terms must be multiplied by the same factor — 10 × 10 = 100, so 7 × 10 = 70, giving 70%. Reading it as 7% describes seats that are nearly empty when they are nearly full. A second mistake is treating a percent as an amount: 150% of a 200-point goal is 1.5 × 200 = 300 points, not 150 points.

level1.stem: 5 out of every 10 kids like soccer best. What percent of the kids is that?
level1.stemEs: A 5 de cada 10 niños les gusta más el fútbol. ¿Qué porcentaje de los niños es eso?
hints: Multiply both terms by 10. Read the number out of 100.
hintsEs: Multiplica los dos términos por 10. Lee el número de cada 100.
level1.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 5 out of 10 Find the scale factor from 10 to 100: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Multiply the part by 10 too: 5 × 10 = 50 Read the percent: 50 out of 100 → 50%
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 5 de cada 10 Halla el factor de escala de 10 a 100: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Multiplica la parte por 10 también: 5 × 10 = 50 Lee el porcentaje: 50 de cada 100 → 50%

level1.stem: A puppy weighs 3 times as much as a kitten. What percent of the kitten's weight is the puppy's weight?
level1.stemEs: Un perrito pesa 3 veces lo que pesa un gatito. ¿Qué porcentaje del peso del gatito es el peso del perrito?
hints: The kitten is the whole, or 100%. The puppy is 3 wholes.
hintsEs: El gatito es el entero, o el 100%. El perrito es 3 enteros.
level1.explanation: Name the whole: kitten → 100% Find the scale factor from 1 to 3: 1 × 3 = 3 Multiply 100% by 3 too: 100 × 3 = 300
level1.explanationEs: Nombra el entero: gatito → 100% Halla el factor de escala de 1 a 3: 1 × 3 = 3 Multiplica 100% por 3 también: 100 × 3 = 300

level1.stem: 9 out of every 10 students brought a lunch. What percent of the students brought a lunch?
level1.stemEs: 9 de cada 10 estudiantes trajeron almuerzo. ¿Qué porcentaje de los estudiantes trajo almuerzo?
hints: Multiply 9 and 10 by 10. Read the number out of 100.
hintsEs: Multiplica 9 y 10 por 10. Lee el número de cada 100.
level1.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 9 out of 10 Find the scale factor from 10 to 100: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Multiply the part by 10 too: 9 × 10 = 90 Read the percent: 90 out of 100 → 90%
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 9 de cada 10 Halla el factor de escala de 10 a 100: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Multiplica la parte por 10 también: 9 × 10 = 90 Lee el porcentaje: 90 de cada 100 → 90%

level1.stem: 8 out of every 10 students like recess best. What percent of the students is that?
level1.stemEs: A 8 de cada 10 estudiantes les gusta más el recreo. ¿Qué porcentaje de los estudiantes es eso?
hints: Multiply both terms by 10 to get a number out of 100.
hintsEs: Multiplica los dos términos por 10 para obtener un número de cada 100.
level1.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 8 out of 10 Find the scale factor from 10 to 100: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Multiply the part by 10 too: 8 × 10 = 80 Read the percent: 80 out of 100 → 80%
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 8 de cada 10 Halla el factor de escala de 10 a 100: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 Multiplica la parte por 10 también: 8 × 10 = 80 Lee el porcentaje: 80 de cada 100 → 80%

level1.stem: A class has 25 students. 9 of them ride the bus. What percent of the class rides the bus?
level1.stemEs: Una clase tiene 25 estudiantes. 9 de ellos van en autobús. ¿Qué porcentaje de la clase va en autobús?
hints: What do you multiply 25 by to get 100? Multiply 9 by the same number.
hintsEs: ¿Por cuánto multiplicas 25 para llegar a 100? Multiplica 9 por el mismo número.
level1.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 9 out of 25 Find the scale factor from 25 to 100: 100 ÷ 25 = 4 Multiply the part by 4 too: 9 × 4 = 36 Read the percent: 36 out of 100 → 36%
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 9 de cada 25 Halla el factor de escala de 25 a 100: 100 ÷ 25 = 4 Multiplica la parte por 4 también: 9 × 4 = 36 Lee el porcentaje: 36 de cada 100 → 36%

level2.stem: Ana says 9 out of every 20 is 9%. Is she right? What percent is 9 out of every 20?
level2.stemEs: Ana dice que 9 de cada 20 es 9%. ¿Tiene razón? ¿Qué porcentaje es 9 de cada 20?
hints: A percent is out of 100, not out of 20. What turns 20 into 100?
hintsEs: Un porcentaje es de cada 100, no de cada 20. ¿Qué convierte 20 en 100?
level2.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 9 out of 20 Find the scale factor from 20 to 100: 100 ÷ 20 = 5 Multiply the part by 5 too: 9 × 5 = 45 Read the percent: 45 out of 100 → 45%
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 9 de cada 20 Halla el factor de escala de 20 a 100: 100 ÷ 20 = 5 Multiplica la parte por 5 también: 9 × 5 = 45 Lee el porcentaje: 45 de cada 100 → 45%

level2.stem: Write 3 out of every 50 as a percent.
hints: What do you multiply 50 by to get 100?
hintsEs: ¿Por cuánto multiplicas 50 para llegar a 100?
level2.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 3 out of 50 Find the scale factor from 50 to 100: 100 ÷ 50 = 2 Multiply the part by 2 too: 3 × 2 = 6 Read the percent: 6 out of 100 → 6%
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 3 de cada 50 Halla el factor de escala de 50 a 100: 100 ÷ 50 = 2 Multiplica la parte por 2 también: 3 × 2 = 6 Lee el porcentaje: 6 de cada 100 → 6%

level2.stem: In a survey, 3 out of every 4 students have a pet. What percent of the students have a pet?
level2.stemEs: En una encuesta, 3 de cada 4 estudiantes tienen una mascota. ¿Qué porcentaje de los estudiantes tiene una mascota?
hints: What do you multiply 4 by to get 100?
hintsEs: ¿Por cuánto multiplicas 4 para llegar a 100?
level2.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 3 out of 4 Find the scale factor from 4 to 100: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 Multiply the part by 25 too: 3 × 25 = 75 Read the percent: 75 out of 100 → 75%
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 3 de cada 4 Halla el factor de escala de 4 a 100: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 Multiplica la parte por 25 también: 3 × 25 = 75 Lee el porcentaje: 75 de cada 100 → 75%

level2.stem: A grid of 100 squares is one whole. Sam shades 2 full grids and 35 squares of one more grid. What percent did Sam shade?
level2.stemEs: Una cuadrícula de 100 cuadros es un entero. Sam sombrea 2 cuadrículas completas y 35 cuadros de otra cuadrícula. ¿Qué porcentaje sombreó Sam?
hints: Each full grid is 100%. Each square is 1%.
hintsEs: Cada cuadrícula completa es el 100%. Cada cuadro es el 1%.
level2.explanation: Find the percent for the full grids: 2 × 100 = 200 Add the squares of the third grid: 200 + 35 = 235 Read the percent: 235 out of 100 → 235%
level2.explanationEs: Halla el porcentaje de las cuadrículas completas: 2 × 100 = 200 Suma los cuadros de la tercera cuadrícula: 200 + 35 = 235 Lee el porcentaje: 235 de cada 100 → 235%

level2.stem: A plant was 20 cm tall. Now it is 30 cm tall. What percent of its first height is its height now?
level2.stemEs: Una planta medía 20 cm. Ahora mide 30 cm. ¿Qué porcentaje de su primera altura es su altura de ahora?
hints: The first height is the whole, or 100%. Multiply both heights by 5.
hintsEs: La primera altura es el entero, o el 100%. Multiplica las dos alturas por 5.
level2.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 30 to 20 Find the scale factor from 20 to 100: 100 ÷ 20 = 5 Multiply the part by 5 too: 30 × 5 = 150 Read the percent: 150 out of 100 → 150%
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 30 a 20 Halla el factor de escala de 20 a 100: 100 ÷ 20 = 5 Multiplica la parte por 5 también: 30 × 5 = 150 Lee el porcentaje: 150 de cada 100 → 150%

level3.stem: A robotics club had a fundraising goal of $500. By Friday, they collected $750. What percent of their goal did they achieve?
choiceFeedback: That is the amount collected BEYOND the goal, not the percent of the goal reached.
That compares $750 to $1000. The goal is $500, and $750 is more than the whole goal.
That would be $625 out of $500. Divide the amount collected by the goal: 750 divided by 500.
level3.explanation: $750 is 1.5 times the whole goal of $500. 1.5 × 100 = 150%, which represents 150% of the goal.

level3.stem: Jen says 21 out of 15 cannot be a percent, because 21 is more than 15. What percent is 21 out of 15?
level3.stemEs: Jen dice que 21 de 15 no puede ser un porcentaje, porque 21 es más que 15. ¿Qué porcentaje es 21 de 15?
hints: 15 is the whole. Divide both terms by 3. Then scale to 100.
hintsEs: 15 es el entero. Divide los dos términos entre 3. Luego escala a 100.
level3.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 21 out of 15 Divide both terms by 3: 21 ÷ 3 = 7; 15 ÷ 3 = 5 Multiply both terms by 20: 7 × 20 = 140; 5 × 20 = 100 Read the percent: 140 out of 100 → 140%
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 21 de cada 15 Divide los dos términos entre 3: 21 ÷ 3 = 7; 15 ÷ 3 = 5 Multiplica los dos términos por 20: 7 × 20 = 140; 5 × 20 = 100 Lee el porcentaje: 140 de cada 100 → 140%

level3.stem: A club planned to sell 80 tickets. It sold 92 tickets. What percent of the plan did the club sell?
level3.stemEs: Un club planeó vender 80 boletos. Vendió 92 boletos. ¿Qué porcentaje del plan vendió el club?
hints: The plan is 100%. Divide both terms by 4, then scale to 100.
hintsEs: El plan es el 100%. Divide los dos términos entre 4 y luego escala a 100.
level3.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 92 to 80 Divide both terms by 4: 92 ÷ 4 = 23; 80 ÷ 4 = 20 Multiply both terms by 5: 23 × 5 = 115; 20 × 5 = 100 Read the percent: 115 out of 100 → 115%
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 92 a 80 Divide los dos términos entre 4: 92 ÷ 4 = 23; 80 ÷ 4 = 20 Multiplica los dos términos por 5: 23 × 5 = 115; 20 × 5 = 100 Lee el porcentaje: 115 de cada 100 → 115%

level3.stem: A recipe needs 2 cups of flour. Kai uses 3.5 cups. What percent of the recipe's flour did Kai use?
level3.stemEs: Una receta necesita 2 tazas de harina. Kai usa 3.5 tazas. ¿Qué porcentaje de la harina de la receta usó Kai?
hints: The recipe's 2 cups are 100%. What turns 2 into 100?
hintsEs: Las 2 tazas de la receta son el 100%. ¿Qué convierte 2 en 100?
level3.explanation: Write the ratio in the table: 3.5 to 2 Find the scale factor from 2 to 100: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Multiply the part by 50 too: 3.5 × 50 = 175 Read the percent: 175 out of 100 → 175%
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la razón en la tabla: 3.5 a 2 Halla el factor de escala de 2 a 100: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Multiplica la parte por 50 también: 3.5 × 50 = 175 Lee el porcentaje: 175 de cada 100 → 175%

level3.stem: Store A sold 45 of its 60 hats. Store B sold 70 of its 80 hats. Store C sold 18 of its 24 hats. Which two stores sold the same percent of their hats?
level3.stemEs: La tienda A vendió 45 de sus 60 gorras. La tienda B vendió 70 de sus 80 gorras. La tienda C vendió 18 de sus 24 gorras. ¿Cuáles dos tiendas vendieron el mismo porcentaje de sus gorras?
hints: Simplify each ratio first. Then scale each one to 100.
hintsEs: Primero simplifica cada razón. Luego escala cada una a 100.
level3.explanation: Write each store's ratio in the table: A: 45 out of 60; B: 70 out of 80; C: 18 out of 24 Simplify each ratio: A: 45/60 = 3/4; B: 70/80 = 7/8; C: 18/24 = 3/4 Scale each one to 100: 3/4 = 75/100 → 75%; 7/8 → 87.5% Compare the percents: A: 75%, B: 87.5%, C: 75%
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la razón de cada tienda en la tabla: A: 45 de cada 60; B: 70 de cada 80; C: 18 de cada 24 Simplifica cada razón: A: 45/60 = 3/4; B: 70/80 = 7/8; C: 18/24 = 3/4 Escala cada una a 100: 3/4 = 75/100 → 75%; 7/8 → 87.5% Compara los porcentajes: A: 75%, B: 87.5%, C: 75%
choicesEs: La tienda A y la tienda C
La tienda A y la tienda B
La tienda B y la tienda C
choiceFeedback: Store A sold 75%, but Store B sold 87.5%.
Store B sold 87.5%, but Store C sold 75%.
